text:
Maya Chen: Quick question — who should own request-level assertions when a request traverses hosted -> dedicated -> private runtimes? we currently have multiple headers and it's causing authz drift.
Luis Ortega: +1 need clarity. do you mean the tenant identity + caller intent bits?
Maya Chen: yes. tenant id, caller (service or user), an assertion version, and a signature that can be validated without KMS calls in-line.
Ivy Patel: I worry about putting a long-lived signature header on every request for perf and leakage. can we use short-lived opaque tokens instead? :thinking_face:
Tom Novak: downside: private deployments want to keep KMS local and not accept externally minted tokens. that means we need a translation step at the private edge.
Maya Chen: proposal sketch: single canonical header X-RW-Assertion that carries a compact JSONB64 payload and an envelope signature type. examples: 
```
X-RW-Assertion: v=1;alg=hs1;payload=eyJ0ZW5hbnQiOiJhY21lIiwicm9sZXMiOlsiYXBpIl19;sig=ab34...
```
Luis Ortega: +1 for one header. Questions: 1) who rotates signing keys? 2) how do we validate in hosted fallback where we don't have customer's KMS?
Ivy Patel: answers: (1) control plane-managed signing keys for platform assertions; (2) for private deployments, we allow an adapter to verify/translate using customer KMS and emit a local assertion.
Tom Novak: that translation is the tricky bit — semantics must be preserved (no privilege elevation). we should define an assertion mapping table so adapters can't accidentally drop flags like "sensitive=false"
Maya Chen: exactly. also need observability: assertion id should be surfaced in traces and logs so we can trace cross-hosting hops without leaking raw creds. propose header fields: tid, sid, flags, exp, aid (assertion id).
Ivy Patel: for expiry, use short TTL (30s-2m) and let proxy refresh where needed. avoids replay.
Luis Ortega: fallback ordering: if runtime can't verify signature it should either 1) reject, 2) request translation, or 3) accept if header signed by platform key and tenant allows it. need config knob per-tenant.
Tom Novak: agree with config knob. Also add audit hook: any time an adapter re-signs or translates, it emits audit event with original assertion id + new id. helps for incident forensics.
Maya Chen: ops-bot can you add a checklist to the hosting-handbook: canonical header format, adapter translation contract, per-tenant knob, audit event schema, trace mapping?
ops-bot: Added TODO 9273 to hosting-handbook -> "Assertion header & adapter contract". assigned to @Maya Chen and @Tom Novak.
Luis Ortega: PR idea: drop a golang verifier lib + a reference node/dotnet shim for adapters. keeps impl consistent.
Ivy Patel: and a small e2e test: hosted -> dedicated -> private where private adapter translates but fails if flags don't match.
Maya Chen: action items: 1) I will draft a short RFC with header grammar + transition plan, 2) Tom + Ivy to write adapter contract, 3) Luis to start verifier lib. target: canary in staging in 3 weeks.
Tom Novak: ack. grouping question — should this be behind a feature flag or rolled tenant-by-tenant?
Maya Chen: tenant-by-tenant. default: opt-out until we've verified translation logic.
Luis Ortega: noted. I'll spin up a spike later today for the verifier API surface.
Ivy Patel: thanks — adding test cases to the eval suite now.
Maya Chen: thanks all. I'll post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
